sections.content:
Population change in Rushmoor in 2032

The population in Rushmoor is projected to increase from 101,003 people in 2022 to 102,135 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 5,807 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Rushmoor
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Rushmoor, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 2,995, with 11,288 births and 8,293 deaths in Rushmoor between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Rushmoor by 3.0%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 5,807, with 65,010 people moving to the area and 70,817 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Rushmoor by 5.7%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,146, with 1,586 people moving to the area and 2,732 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Rushmoor by 1.1%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 4,983, with 11,035 people moving to the area and 6,052 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Rushmoor by 4.9%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Rushmoor in 2032

The median age in Rushmoor is projected to rise from 38 years in 2022 to 40 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 17% of the population in Rushmoor are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 14% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Rushmoor between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Rushmoor is projected to stay the same, at around 66%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 217 to 240 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Rushmoor?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 22% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Rushmoor between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
